questions.q: Who gave Jeremiah this message?
questions.a: Yahweh gave Jeremiah this message.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to proclaim his message?
questions.a: At the gate of the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: What does Yahweh promise to do for the people if they make their ways and deeds good?
questions.a: He will let them continue to live in that place.

questions.q: What must the people do in order for Yahweh to let them stay in the land?
questions.a: They must make their ways and deeds good by practicing justice.

questions.q: What must the people not do if they want Yahweh to let them stay in the land?
questions.a: They must not exploit the weak, kill the innocent, or worship false gods.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the words the people are trusting in?
questions.a: He says they are trusting in words of deceit that will not benefit them.

questions.q: What sins does Yahweh accuse the people of committing?
questions.a: He accuses them of stealing, murdering, committing adultery, swearing falsely, and worshiping Baal and other gods.

questions.q: What do the people say after they do things they know Yahweh hates?
questions.a: They go to the temple and say that they are safe.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare his temple to?
questions.a: He compares it to a hideout for robbers.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh want the people to think about Shiloh?
questions.a: He wanted them to remember that he would do to them what he had done to Shiloh, because they were guilty of the same sins committed by the people of Shiloh.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh compare the people of Judah to when he says he will cast them out?
questions.a: He compares them to their brothers, the people of Ephraim, whom he had already cast out.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh not listen to Jeremiah’s prayers?
questions.a: He will not listen because he has decided to destroy the Israelites.

questions.q: Where does Yahweh say the people are doing wicked things?
questions.a: In the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh destroy the people?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy the people because they are worshiping other gods.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh say is really being hurt by the people’s actions?
questions.a: He says the people are hurting themselves, to their own shame.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will pour out on the people, animals, trees, and crops?
questions.a: He says he will pour out his anger, which will burn like a fire that cannot be put out.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people to do with their burnt offerings and sacrifices?
questions.a: He tells them to add their burnt offerings to their other sacrifices and eat the meat themselves.

questions.q: What did Yahweh not command the people’s ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt?
questions.a: He did not command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices.

questions.q: What command did Yahweh give the people when they left Egypt?
questions.a: He commanded them to listen to his voice.

questions.q: How did the people’s ancestors respond to Yahweh?
questions.a: They did not listen to him; they followed the stubborn plans of their own evil hearts and turned away from him.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh send to the people from the time they left Egypt until now?
questions.a: He sent his servants, the prophets, to them again and again.

questions.q: What did the people do when Yahweh sent prophets?
questions.a: They did not listen or pay attention. They did evil.

questions.q: How will the people respond when Jeremiah speaks and calls to them?
questions.a: They will not listen to him, and they will not answer him.

questions.q: What is the prophet to say to them?
questions.a: He is to say to them that this is a nation that does not listen to the voice of Yahweh.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh tell the people to cut off their hair and mourn?
questions.a: He tells them to do this because he has rejected and abandoned this generation of people who have angered him.

questions.q: What have the people of Judah set up in Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: They have set up their disgusting idols in his temple, defiling it.

questions.q: Why did the people build high places at Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom?
questions.a: They built them so they could burn their sons and daughters in fire there.

questions.q: What will that valley be called instead of Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom?
questions.a: It will be called the Valley of Slaughter.

questions.q: What will become of the corpses of this people?
questions.a: Birds and wild animals will eat them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
questions.a: He will stop the sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of brides and grooms; the land will be destroyed.

commentary.text: Confidence in the temple is vain. (Jer. 7:1-16) The provocation by persisting in idolatry. (Jer. 7:17-20) God justifies his dealings with them. (Jer. 7:21-28) And threatens vengeance. (Jer. 7:29-34)

Jer. 7:1-16 No observances, professions, or supposed revelations, will profit, if men do not amend their ways and their doings. None can claim an interest in free salvation, who allow themselves in the practice of known sin, or live in the neglect of known duty. They thought that the temple they profaned would be their protection. But all who continue in sin because grace has abounded, or that grace may abound, make Christ the minister of sin; and the cross of Christ, rightly understood, forms the most effectual remedy to such poisonous sentiments. The Son of God gave himself for our transgressions, to show the excellence of the Divine law, and the evil of sin. Never let us think we may do wickedness without suffering for it.

Jer. 7:17-20 The Jews took pride in showing zeal for their idols. Let us learn to be earnest in the service of our God, even from this bad example. Let us think it an honour to be employed in any work for God. Let us be as diligent ourselves, and as careful to teach our children the truths of God, as many are to teach the mysteries of iniquity. The direct tendency of this sin is malice against God, but it will hurt themselves. And they shall find there is no escaping. God's wrath is fire unquenchable.

Jer. 7:21-28 God shows that obedience was required of them. That which God commanded was, Hearken diligently to the voice of the Lord thy God. The promise is very encouraging. Let God's will be your rule, and his favour shall be your happiness. God was displeased with disobedience. We understand the gospel as little as the Jews understood the law, if we think that even the sacrifice of Christ lessens our obligation to obey.

Jer. 7:29-34 In token both of sorrow and of slavery, Jerusalem must be degraded, and separated from God, as she had been separated to him. The heart is the place in which God has chosen to put his name; but if sin has the innermost and uppermost place there, we pollute the temple of the Lord. The destruction of Jerusalem appears here very terrible. The slain shall be many; they having made it the place of their sin. Evil pursues sinners, even after death. Those who will not, by the grace of God, be cured of vain mirth, shall, by the justice of God, be deprived of all mirth. How many ruin their health and property without complaining, when engaged in Satan's service! May we learn to relish holy joys, and to sit loose to all others though lawful.
